standard_prerequisites.name: A dominant morphism of integral schemes of the same dimension is finite in codimension one
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, label lemma-finite-in-codimension-one, invoked at proof line 2662
standard_prerequisites.use: At the generic point of an integral closed subscheme of codimension one it lets the target be replaced by an affine neighbourhood over which the morphism is finite.

standard_prerequisites.name: Norm compatibility of orders in a finite extension of dimension one
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, label algebra-lemma-finite-extension-dim-1, invoked at proof line 2680
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the equality between the order at a height one prime of the norm and the sum over the primes above it of the residue degrees times the orders, which is exactly the coefficient comparison.

core_obligations: Reduce to a coefficient comparison: fix an integral closed subscheme of codimension one and use the codimension one finiteness statement to shrink the target to an affine neighbourhood of its generic point, so that the morphism becomes finite between affine integral schemes (proof lines 2658-2665).

Translate to algebra: write the two schemes as spectra of Noetherian domains with a finite injective map of fraction fields, and identify the coefficient in the divisor of the norm with the order of the norm at the corresponding height one prime, and the coefficient in the pushforward with the sum over the primes above it of the residue degrees times the orders (proof lines 2666-2678).
Conclude by the norm compatibility statement for finite extensions of dimension one (proof lines 2679-2680).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a finite morphism over an affine neighbourhood of a codimension one point (proof lines 2658-2665).
Identify both coefficients in ring theoretic terms (proof lines 2666-2678).
Apply the norm compatibility statement (proof lines 2679-2680).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the pushforward of the divisor of a rational function along a dominant proper morphism between integral schemes of the same dimension as the divisor of the norm of that function (statement lines 2644-2656, tag 02RT). The proof reduces to comparing coefficients at an integral closed subscheme of codimension one, uses the codimension one finiteness statement to make the morphism finite over an affine neighbourhood, rewrites both coefficients in ring theoretic terms as an order and as a sum of residue degrees times orders, and concludes with the norm compatibility statement for finite extensions of dimension one. The reduction to the finite case is the substance, so the claim is H2.
